lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Quietly, please. There are twelve candles burning in this shrine, and one for each name you will learn to say.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: I keep the Shrine of Echoes. When Hollowmere loses someone, I make sure the town does not lose them twice.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: First the body goes down into the dark, and then the name goes out of the ledger, and then out of the toasts, and then out of the mouths. I keep the candle so the last of those never happens.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Grief that is not tended goes underground and waits. That is a lesson this town is about to learn again, I think.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the candles.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: I lit the thirteenth candle last night. Foreman Hollis gets a taller one — he carried more of us than most.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: The town calls you warden. I call you the one who carries the candles down. Try not to become one of them.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: You count well. The twelfth went out two nights ago — it guttered on its own, with the shutters closed.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Relit it did, at dawn, burning backward. I have not told anyone but you. A thing that gives light backward is not our grief anymore.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: You read a letter down there. I can see it in how you stand. Whose was it?

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Bring the words back to me someday. The shrine keeps names; let it keep a sentence or two as well.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: I prayed for the miners' rest. The shrine heard me and answered wrong. Now they walk.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Understand what I am asking, warden: do not bring them up here to be saved. Some things the shrine cannot tend. What wears my neighbours is one of them.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: The echoes in this shrine have started to arrive before the words that cause them. Sit with that a while.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: I have stopped counting candles. I count the ones that stay lit instead. It is a shorter prayer.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: Whatever was listening down there has turned its ear away. The shrine is only a room again. I will miss being heard.

lines.speaker: Sister Ash
lines.text: The candles are lit. Say your names while they hold.
